charge_limit_crate.description: Max charge C-rate; rows = temperature, cols = SOC. Rows below 0 degC are zero because the datasheet curve ends at 0 degC with C-rate 0 and the charge hard cutoff is at 0 degC. Above 80 % SOC the limit tapers linearly to the value of the 100 % SOC column.

discharge_limit_crate.description: Generic continuous discharge C-rate for an LFP home battery. 0.5C in the normal range, derated near the low and high temperature ends. Peak discharge (typically around 1C) is deliberately not represented; only the continuous rating is stored, which is the safe value for controller-side power limiting.

charge_efficiency.description: Generic one-way DC charge efficiency of an LFP battery pack (cells and BMS) versus absolute C-rate. Losses grow with current (I^2 R), so efficiency falls slowly with C-rate. AC/DC conversion losses are not included; they belong to the inverter settings (ac_to_dc_efficiency).

discharge_efficiency.description: Generic one-way DC discharge efficiency of an LFP battery pack (cells and BMS) versus absolute C-rate. The curve ends at the 0.5C continuous discharge rating of this profile; higher C-rates are clamped to the last point. DC/AC conversion losses are not included; they belong to the inverter settings (dc_to_ac_efficiency).

hard_cutoffs.description: Charge is inhibited strictly below 0 degC and strictly above 60 degC. At exactly 0 degC and exactly 60 degC the charge map returns 0.0, so charging is effectively disabled there too. Discharge is inhibited strictly below -10 degC and strictly above 60 degC; the discharge map already reaches 0.0 at both ends, so the hard cutoff only governs whether the accessor returns None or 0.0.
